newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market Eurobonds end week on low note.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market Eurobonds end week on low note.

text.p: Spreads on emerging market Eurobonds widened by up to 50 basis points in the last week amid turbulence in world bond markets, bankers said on Friday.
"Latin American (dollar) Eurobond spreads are up to 50 b.p. wider on the week, Eastern European bonds around 15 b.p wider," a debt trader at a European bank said.
"We expect the market to remain unsettled until the release of non-farm payrolls next Friday," he said.
Selling of emerging market paper was triggered by comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that the Fed could tighten monetary policy before evidence of inflation emerges.
Markets expect U.S. interest rates to rise, perhaps as early as the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
U.S. employment data for February is due to be released on March 7 and will be closely watched for signs of economic growth and wage pressures.
"Smaller, corporate bonds have moved a bit less than the sovereign benchmarks, but the emerging market sector is under a lot of pressure," a dealer at a U.S. bank said.
"A lot of banks had Mexico and Argentina paper on their books in anticipation of spreads continuing to rally. Now they are selling and caused a sharp price move," he said.

Mexico's 2026 dollar global bond was trading at around 350 b.p. over U.S. Treasury bonds, up from around 315 on Tuesday. Argentina's 2017 dollar global bond was quoted at around 386 b.p. over from a 240 b.p. spread on Tuesday.
Worries Mexico might be not be certified by the U.S. had added negative pressure, dealers said.

By Saturday, U.S. President Bill Clinton must decide whether he will approve or disqualify Mexico and 31 other countries as allies in the war on drugs. Countries that fail the test may be subject to economic and trade sanctions.
Dealers said there were few new issues in the pipeline for next week, with borrowers likely to want to wait to see how the market evolved before raising new money.
